says: An integration law calls control through Reflect.apply typed Effect.Effect<Response, unknown>, which erases its services, so PR 1644 made control require Dispatcher and pnpm typecheck passed while the law died at run time; under 0602 the law runs only on main, where fail-fast hid it behind another red law, and the same erased call shape sits in readers.laws.test.ts lines 272 and 285. A cheap check would have caught it on the pull request: call a function with a known signature directly in a law, and keep Reflect.apply for a member picked at run time (0554 leaves Reflect.apply undecided).
proof: `rg -n "Reflect\.apply\(control" next` prints 4 lines (dev-secrets 482 and 492, readers 272 and 285). Main's full run https://github.com/kamp-us/tea-fabrika/actions/runs/44410508388 leg 3 fails the law at line 587 (expected false to be true); https://github.com/kamp-us/tea-fabrika/actions/runs/44415751425 at 180b1345a passes it and https://github.com/kamp-us/tea-fabrika/actions/runs/44415755034 at 63e05f085 (PR 1644) fails it. control.ts line 140 reads `yield* Dispatcher`; the law provides only `logger` at line 502.
cost: Any service a later change adds to control, or to another function a law calls through Reflect.apply, merges green and shows only on main's full run as a sev1.
